- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is rising, model often overreacts; cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction of 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion rule: target 1–2 std dev below recent 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward trends in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.75 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags; add 0.5–1.0% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
